description: To understand the concepts of cloud computing. To learn taxonomy of virtualization techniques. To learn cloud computing architecture. To acquire knowledge on cloud application platforms. To understand cloud networking issues.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Cloud Computing
syllabus.body: Cloud computing (NIST model), cloud service provider properties, characteristics & disadvantages, benefits of cloud computing, cloud vs. cluster vs. grid computing, role of open standards.

syllabus.title: Cloud Computing Architecture and Service Models
syllabus.body: Cloud computing architecture compared with traditional client/server architecture, role of networks and web services; Infrastructure/Hardware as a Service, Platform as a Service, Software as a Service; public, private, hybrid and community clouds; economics of the cloud.

syllabus.title: Virtualization
syllabus.body: Need for virtualization, types of hardware virtualization: full, partial, para virtualization; desktop, software, memory, storage, data and network virtualization.

syllabus.title: Service Management and Security
syllabus.body: Service Level Agreements (SLAs), billing & accounting, scalability & cloud services, database & data stores in cloud, large scale data processing; infrastructure/network/host/application-level security, data security and privacy issues, identity & access management, authentication in cloud computing.

outcomes: Understand the concept of virtualization and how this has enabled the development of Cloud Computing.
Know the fundamentals of cloud, cloud architectures and types of services in cloud.
Understand scaling, cloud security and network management.
referenceBooks: Barrie Sosinsky, Cloud Computing Bible, Wiley-India, 2010.
Rajkumar Buyya, James Broberg, Andrzej M. Goscinski (eds.), Cloud Computing: Principles and Paradigms, Wiley, 2011.
